_comentario: Escenarios de conversación con la IA (Fase 3). Cada uno es una situación cerrada: la profesora hace un papel (role), abre con una frase (opening) y el alumno tiene metas (targets). 'watch' son las trampas típicas del hispanohablante en esa situación: la IA las corrige en español. Todos los campos son obligatorios (checkContent).

helpCommon.en: Sorry, could you repeat that, please?
helpCommon.es: Cuando no alcanzaste a oír. Pide repetir sin cortar la charla.

helpCommon.en: Could you speak more slowly, please?
helpCommon.es: Cuando va muy rápido. 'More slowly', no 'more slow'.

helpCommon.en: How do you say ___ in English?
helpCommon.es: Para preguntar una palabra que te falta. 'How', no 'What'.
Para preguntar qué significa algo que ella dijo. Lleva 'does' y el verbo sin -s.
Dilo sin miedo: en inglés se usa mucho y no suena grosero.
Para que te lo escriba y lo veas.

scenarios.title: Conocer a alguien
scenarios.goalEs: Preséntate: tu nombre, de dónde eres, tu edad y qué haces. Hazle una pregunta a ella.
scenarios.role: You are chatting with a new student at a language exchange in a park. You are friendly and curious.
scenarios.opening: Hi! I don't think we've met. I'm {teacher}. What's your name?
targets: I'm a ... / I work as a ...
watch: 'I have 25 years' → se dice 'I'm 25 years old'
'My sister is doctor' → hace falta el artículo: 'is a doctor'
'I am agree' → 'I agree', sin am
'How do you call yourself?' → 'What's your name?'

help.en: What's your name? / Where are you from?
help.es: Preguntas con 'What' y 'Where' + el verbo be al principio.

help.en: I'm ___ and I'm from ___.
help.es: Con el verbo be, no con 'have': la edad y el origen van con 'I am'.

help.en: How old are you?
help.es: Literalmente '¿qué tan viejo eres?'. Nunca 'How many years do you have?'.

help.en: What do you do?
help.es: Así se pregunta a qué se dedica alguien. Lleva 'do' dos veces.

help.en: I work as a ___. / I'm a ___.
help.es: Las profesiones SIEMPRE llevan 'a' o 'an' delante.

help.en: Nice to meet you.
help.es: Para cerrar la presentación. No 'Nice to meet to you'.

scenarios.title: En la cafetería
scenarios.goalEs: Pide un café y algo de comer, pregunta cuánto cuesta y dile si es para llevar.
scenarios.role: You are a barista at a small coffee shop. Take the order, ask about size and milk, say the price, and ask if it's for here or to go.
scenarios.opening: Hi there, welcome! What can I get for you today?
watch: 'I want a coffee' suena a exigencia → 'I'd like a coffee' o 'Can I have a coffee?'
'For carry' / 'to take' → 'to go'
'How much cost?' → 'How much is it?'
'Give me' sin please suena brusco

help.en: Can I have a ___, please?
help.es: La forma normal de pedir. 'Can I have', no 'I want'.

help.en: I'd like a ___, please.
help.es: Más suave todavía. 'I'd like' = 'I would like'.

help.en: How much is it? / How much are they?
help.es: 'Is' para una cosa, 'are' para varias.

help.en: Do you have ___?
help.es: Preguntas con 'do' al principio; el verbo se queda sin -s.

help.en: Can I pay by card?
help.es: 'By card', 'in cash'. Cada uno con su preposición.

help.en: That's all, thank you.
help.es: Para cerrar el pedido.

scenarios.title: Preguntar el camino
scenarios.goalEs: Estás perdido. Pregunta cómo llegar a la estación de tren y confirma las indicaciones.
scenarios.role: You are a local person on the street. Give simple directions to the train station: go straight, turn left at the bank, it's on the right, about five minutes.
scenarios.opening: Hello! You look a little lost. Can I help you?
targets: Excuse me, how do I get to ...?
On the left / on the right
watch: 'Where is the station?' está bien, pero 'Where the station is?' no
'Excuse me' para pedir ayuda; 'sorry' es para disculparse
'Far' no lleva 'of': 'Is it far?' o 'Is it far from here?'
'In the left' → 'on the left'

help.en: Excuse me, where is the ___?
help.es: 'Excuse me' para empezar; 'where is' pegado al principio.

help.en: How do I get to ___?
help.es: La pregunta más útil de todas para orientarte.

help.en: Is it far from here?
help.es: Pregunta cerrada: empieza por el verbo be.

help.en: Is there a ___ near here?
help.es: 'Is there' = '¿hay?'. En plural, 'Are there'.

help.en: Turn left / turn right / go straight.
help.es: Órdenes: el verbo solo, sin sujeto.

help.en: Thank you very much!
help.es: Para cerrar cuando ya te explicaron.

scenarios.title: En una tienda de ropa
scenarios.goalEs: Busca una camiseta: pregunta por tu talla, otro color y el precio. Decide si la compras.
scenarios.role: You are a shop assistant in a clothes store. Help the customer find a T-shirt: ask the size, offer colors, say the price, and offer the fitting room.
scenarios.opening: Hi! Are you looking for anything in particular today?
watch: 'I search a T-shirt' → 'I'm looking for a T-shirt'
'Medium size' se dice 'a medium' o 'size medium'
'Can I prove it?' → 'Can I try it on?' (probar ropa es try on)
'Blue color' → solo 'blue'

help.en: I'm looking for ___.
help.es: Presente continuo: be + verbo con -ing. 'I'm looking', no 'I look'.

help.en: Do you have this in ___?
help.es: Para pedir otra talla o color, con 'do' al principio.

help.en: Can I try it on?
help.es: 'Try on' se usa para ropa; el 'it' va en la mitad.

help.en: It's too big / too small.
help.es: 'Too' = demasiado. 'Very big' es solo 'muy grande'.

help.en: How much does it cost?
help.es: Con 'does', el verbo va sin -s: 'cost', no 'costs'.

help.en: I'll take it.
help.es: 'Me lo llevo'. 'I'll' = 'I will', decisión del momento.

scenarios.title: Llegar al hotel
scenarios.goalEs: Haz el check-in: di que tienes una reserva, deletrea tu apellido, pregunta por el desayuno y el wifi.
scenarios.role: You are a hotel receptionist. Ask for the name and the reservation, confirm two nights, explain breakfast time and the wifi password, and give the room number.
scenarios.opening: Good evening, welcome to the Park Hotel. Do you have a reservation?
targets: I have a reservation under the name ...
Thank you, have a good night.
watch: 'I have a reserve' → 'I have a reservation'
'The breakfast is included?' → 'Is breakfast included?' (la pregunta invierte el orden)
'What hour is the breakfast?' → 'What time is breakfast?'
'Actually' no significa actualmente: es 'de hecho'

help.en: I have a reservation under the name ___.
help.es: 'Under the name', no 'in the name'.

help.en: What time is breakfast? / What time is check-out?
help.es: 'What time', no 'At what hour'.

help.en: Could I have a room with ___?
help.es: 'Could' es más formal que 'can'; sirve en un hotel.

help.en: Is breakfast included?
help.es: Pregunta cerrada con be al principio.

help.en: The ___ isn't working.
help.es: Para decir que algo está dañado. Presente continuo con 'isn't'.

help.en: Can you help me, please?
help.es: Pedir ayuda directo y educado.

scenarios.title: En el consultorio
scenarios.goalEs: Cuéntale al médico qué te pasa, desde cuándo, y entiende lo que te manda.
scenarios.role: You are a doctor at a walk-in clinic. Ask what the problem is, how long it has lasted, whether the patient has taken anything, and give simple advice and a prescription. Be warm but efficient.
scenarios.opening: Good morning. Please have a seat. What seems to be the problem?
watch: 'I have pain in my head' → 'I have a headache'
'Since three days' → 'For three days' (duración lleva for)
'I am constipated' significa estreñido, no resfriado → 'I have a cold'
'Take a medicine' → 'take medicine' o 'take a pill'

help.en: I have a headache / a sore throat / a fever.
help.es: Los síntomas más comunes. Fíjate que headache lleva 'a'.

help.en: It started three days ago.
help.es: 'Ago' va al final y se usa con pasado simple.

help.en: I've had it for a week.
help.es: 'For' + duración. Con present perfect porque sigue.

help.en: It hurts when I swallow.
help.es: 'It hurts', no 'it pains'.

help.en: Do I have to take anything?
help.es: 'Have to' para preguntar si es obligatorio.

help.en: How often should I take it?
help.es: 'How often' = cada cuánto.

scenarios.title: Devolver algo que salió malo
scenarios.goalEs: Explica qué compraste, qué le pasa, y consigue que te lo cambien o te devuelvan el dinero.
scenarios.role: You work at the customer service desk of a store. A customer wants to return something. Ask what happened, when they bought it, whether they have the receipt, and offer an exchange before a refund. Be polite but not immediately agreeable.
scenarios.opening: Hello, how can I help you today?
targets: I bought this ... and it doesn't work
watch: 'I want my money' suena agresivo → 'I'd like a refund, please'
'It's broken since yesterday' → 'It broke yesterday' o 'It's been broken since yesterday'
'Ticket' es de bus o cine; el papel de la compra es 'receipt'
'Change it' a secas → 'exchange it'

help.en: I bought this here last week.
help.es: Pasado simple con 'last week'.

help.en: It doesn't work / It stopped working.
help.es: Las dos formas de decir que no sirve.

help.en: I'd like a refund, please.
help.es: 'Refund' = devolución del dinero.

help.en: Can I exchange it for another one?
help.es: 'Exchange it for', con for.

help.en: Here's the receipt.
help.es: 'Receipt' — la p no se pronuncia: «ri-SIIT».

help.en: Could I speak to the manager, please?
help.es: Para subir de nivel sin sonar grosero.

scenarios.title: Ver un apartamento
scenarios.goalEs: Pregunta todo lo que necesitas saber antes de alquilar: qué incluye, cuánto cuesta, qué reglas hay.
scenarios.role: You are a landlord showing a small apartment. Describe the rooms, answer questions about rent, bills, furniture and rules, and ask the person about themselves. Mention that another person is also interested.
scenarios.opening: Come in, come in. So this is the living room — it gets a lot of light in the morning.
watch: 'How much is the rent?' no 'How much costs the rent?'
'There is two bedrooms' → 'There ARE two bedrooms'
'It has a washing machine?' → 'Is there a washing machine?'
'Furnitures' no existe: furniture no lleva -s

help.en: How much is the rent per month?
help.es: 'Per month' o 'a month', las dos valen.

help.en: Are the bills included?
help.es: 'Bills' = servicios. En plural.

help.en: Is there a washing machine?
help.es: 'Is there' para una cosa, 'Are there' para varias.

help.en: How many bedrooms are there?
help.es: 'How many' porque los cuartos se cuentan.

help.en: Am I allowed to have pets?
help.es: 'Allowed to' = permitido. Más natural que 'can I'.

help.en: When would it be available?
help.es: 'Would' lo vuelve más educado.

scenarios.title: Hacer planes con un amigo
scenarios.goalEs: Ponte de acuerdo para hacer algo el fin de semana: propón, rechaza algo con una razón, y cierra la hora y el sitio.
scenarios.role: You are a friend making weekend plans. Suggest two or three things, react to their ideas, mention you are busy Saturday morning, and agree on a time and place. Keep it casual and friendly.
scenarios.opening: Hey! So, are you doing anything this weekend?
watch: 'What do you do this weekend?' pregunta por tu trabajo → 'What are you doing this weekend?'
'How about to go?' → 'How about going?' (después de about va -ing)
'I have to work' está bien, pero 'I must work' suena exagerado entre amigos
'At Saturday' → 'On Saturday'

help.en: What are you doing this weekend?
help.es: Continuo para planes ya hechos.

help.en: How about going to the movies?
help.es: Después de 'how about', el verbo lleva -ing.

help.en: I'd rather do something outside.
help.es: 'I'd rather' + verbo pelado.

help.en: I can't on Saturday morning, I'm working.
help.es: Los días con 'on'.

help.en: Does seven work for you?
help.es: Muy natural para proponer una hora.

help.en: Let's meet at the entrance.
help.es: 'Let's' + verbo pelado.

scenarios.title: Perdiste la conexión
scenarios.goalEs: Explica qué pasó, averigua qué opciones tienes, y consigue que te reubiquen.
scenarios.role: You work at an airline help desk. A passenger missed their connection. Ask what happened, check options, explain there is a flight tomorrow morning and one tonight with a stop, and mention the hotel voucher policy. Be calm and professional.
scenarios.opening: Next, please. How can I help you?
watch: 'I lost my flight' → 'I missed my flight' (lose es perder un objeto)
'The flight had delay' → 'The flight was delayed'
'I am waiting since two hours' → 'I have been waiting for two hours'
'What I can do?' → 'What can I do?'

help.en: I missed my connection to Bogotá.
help.es: 'Miss' para perder un vuelo o un bus.

help.en: My first flight was delayed.
help.es: 'Was delayed', en pasiva.

help.en: Is there another flight tonight?
help.es: 'Is there' para preguntar si existe.

help.en: What are my options?
help.es: Frase corta y muy útil cuando algo falla.

help.en: Do you provide a hotel?
help.es: 'Provide' = dar, en contexto formal.

help.en: How long is the layover?
help.es: 'Layover' = la escala.

scenarios.title: Tu primer día de trabajo
scenarios.goalEs: Preséntate, pregunta cómo funcionan las cosas y entiende qué se espera de ti.
scenarios.role: You are a friendly team lead welcoming a new colleague on their first day. Introduce yourself, explain the schedule and the lunch routine, ask about their background, and tell them who to ask for help.
scenarios.opening: You must be the new one — welcome! I'm Sarah, I lead the team. Did you find the office okay?
watch: 'I have 30 years' → 'I'm 30 years old'
'I work here since Monday' → 'I've worked here since Monday'
'Actually' significa 'en realidad', no 'actualmente' → 'currently'
'I am agree' → 'I agree'

help.en: Nice to meet you. I'm ...
help.es: Fórmula completa, no solo el nombre.

help.en: What time do we usually start?
help.es: 'What time' + do + sujeto + verbo.

help.en: Who should I ask about the computer?
help.es: 'Should' para pedir orientación.

help.en: I used to work at a hospital.
help.es: 'Used to' para un trabajo anterior.

help.en: Could you show me where the kitchen is?
help.es: Ojo al orden: 'where the kitchen is', no 'where is the kitchen'.

help.en: Sorry, I didn't catch your name.
help.es: Para pedir que repitan un nombre sin pena.

scenarios.title: Entrevista de trabajo
scenarios.goalEs: Habla de tu experiencia, explica por qué te interesa el puesto y responde la pregunta incómoda.
scenarios.role: You are interviewing a candidate for a job. Ask about their experience, why they want the role, a strength and a weakness, and one difficult question about a gap or a mistake. Push gently for concrete examples rather than generalities.
scenarios.opening: Thanks for coming in. To start — tell me a little about yourself and what you've been doing recently.
targets: In my last job I was responsible for ...
I'm interested in this role because ...
watch: 'I have 5 years working here' → 'I've been working here for 5 years'
'I have experience in manage teams' → 'in managing teams' (tras preposición va -ing)
'I am responsible of' → 'responsible FOR'
'Assist to a meeting' → 'attend a meeting'

help.en: I've been working as a ... for three years.
help.es: Present perfect continuo: empezó antes y sigue.

help.en: In my last job I was responsible for ...
help.es: 'Responsible FOR', siempre con for.

help.en: What attracted me to this role is ...
help.es: Suena más preparado que 'I like'.

help.en: For example, last year I ...
help.es: Dar un ejemplo concreto es lo que más pesa en una entrevista.

help.en: I'd say my main strength is ...
help.es: 'I'd say' suaviza el autoelogio.

help.en: That's something I'm still working on.
help.es: La mejor forma de contestar por una debilidad.

scenarios.title: Ponerse de acuerdo
scenarios.goalEs: Defiende tu propuesta, admite lo que tiene de bueno la otra, y llega a un punto medio.
scenarios.role: You are a colleague who disagrees about how to spend a small team budget. You want new equipment; push back on their idea with reasons, concede one point, and look for a compromise. Do not give in too quickly.
scenarios.opening: Look, I've been thinking about the budget, and honestly I think we should put it all into new equipment.
watch: 'I am agree' → 'I agree' (agree es verbo, no adjetivo)
'I am not agree' → 'I don't agree' o 'I disagree'
'In my personal opinion I think' es redundante → 'I think' o 'In my opinion'
'Depends of' → 'depends ON'

help.en: I see your point, but I'm not sure that's the priority.
help.es: Conceder antes de discrepar: suena mucho mejor.

help.en: I don't agree, and here's why.
help.es: 'I don't agree', nunca 'I am not agree'.

help.en: What if we split it?
help.es: 'What if' + presente para proponer.

help.en: It depends on how long it lasts.
help.es: 'Depends ON', con on.

help.en: Couldn't we do both?
help.es: La pregunta negativa suaviza la propuesta.

help.en: Fair enough — let's try it your way.
help.es: Para ceder sin quedar debajo.

scenarios.title: Contar cómo lo resolviste
scenarios.goalEs: Cuenta un problema que tuviste, qué habías intentado antes, y cómo terminó.
scenarios.role: You are a friend catching up. Ask about a problem they had recently, and keep asking follow-up questions: what had happened before, what they tried, what they would do differently. React naturally.
scenarios.opening: You mentioned last time that something went wrong at work. What happened in the end?
targets: If I could do it again, I'd ...
watch: 'I was working there since 2020' → 'I had been working there since 2020'
'At the end' significa al final físico → 'In the end' para el desenlace
'I realized of' → 'I realized' (sin of)
'Support' no es soportar/aguantar → 'put up with'

help.en: It all started when ...
help.es: La mejor forma de abrir una historia.

help.en: I had already tried ... before that.
help.es: Pasado perfecto: lo anterior a lo anterior.

help.en: While I was waiting, they called.
help.es: Fondo en continuo, golpe en pasado simple.

help.en: In the end, it worked out.
help.es: 'In the end' = al final de la historia.

help.en: If I could do it again, I'd ask sooner.
help.es: Segundo condicional para el arrepentimiento.

help.en: To be honest, I was pretty annoyed.
help.es: Para meter emoción sin exagerar.

scenarios.title: Un trámite que se complica
scenarios.goalEs: Explica qué te dijeron antes, señala la contradicción, y consigue una solución sin pelear.
scenarios.role: You are a bank clerk. The customer was told something different by a colleague last week. Explain the rule, ask for a document they probably don't have, and only after they insist politely, offer an alternative you can authorize.
scenarios.opening: Let me look at your account... Hmm. I'm afraid we can't process this without proof of address.
targets: Last week I was told that ...
watch: 'They said me' → 'They told me' (tell lleva persona, say no)
'He said that I have to' → en indirecto retrocede: 'he said I had to'
'I'm here since 20 minutes' → 'I've been here for 20 minutes'
Subir la voz no ayuda; en inglés se insiste con 'Could you...' y 'Is there any way...'

help.en: Last week I was told that ...
help.es: Pasiva: útil cuando no sabes el nombre de quién te atendió.

help.en: She told me I only needed my ID.
help.es: 'Told me' con persona. Y 'needed', que retrocede.

help.en: Is there any way around this?
help.es: Pide una salida sin acusar a nadie.

help.en: Could you check with your colleague?
help.es: 'Could you' es lo más educado sin ser sumiso.

help.en: I understand it's not your fault, but ...
help.es: Baja la tensión y mantiene la presión.

help.en: What would you do in my position?
help.es: Los convierte en aliados. Funciona sorprendentemente bien.

scenarios.title: Dar tu opinión sobre un tema
scenarios.goalEs: Toma una postura, dale dos razones, reconoce el otro lado y cierra.
scenarios.role: You are discussing whether people should work from home. Take the opposite position from whatever the learner takes, give reasons, and ask them to justify theirs with examples. Keep it friendly, not hostile.
scenarios.opening: I was reading something about remote work this morning. Do you think people are actually more productive at home?
watch: 'I think that yes' → 'I think so'
'In one hand / in other hand' → 'On the one hand / on the other hand'
'Is very important the family' → 'Family is very important' (el inglés necesita el sujeto delante)
'People is' → 'People ARE'

help.en: I think so, mainly because ...
help.es: 'I think so' para contestar que sí a una opinión.

help.en: On the one hand ... on the other hand ...
help.es: Las dos con 'on'. Es la estructura que más se falla.

help.en: For instance, in my own case ...
help.es: 'For instance' = 'for example', suena más cuidado.

help.en: That's a fair point, but ...
help.es: Reconocer el otro lado sube el nivel de tu inglés al instante.

help.en: It depends on the kind of job.
help.es: Matizar vale más que tener razón.

help.en: Overall, I'd say it works for some people.
help.es: 'Overall' para cerrar.

scenarios.title: Explicar a qué te dedicas
scenarios.goalEs: Explícale tu trabajo o tu estudio a alguien que no sabe nada del tema, sin tecnicismos.
scenarios.role: You are someone at a party with no background in the learner's field. Be curious and ask simple but persistent questions: what it is, why it matters, what a normal day looks like, and what the hardest part is. Ask them to explain anything technical in simple words.
scenarios.opening: So, what do you do? And I should warn you — I know absolutely nothing about it.
targets: The point of it is to ...
watch: 'I am studying a doctorate' → 'I'm doing a PhD'
'Investigation' es de policía; la científica es 'research'
'Research' no lleva -s: 'my research', nunca 'researches'
'Carrera' universitaria es 'degree', no 'career'

help.en: Basically, I work on ...
help.es: 'Basically' avisa que viene la versión simple.

help.en: It's a bit like ... , but for ...
help.es: La comparación es lo que hace entender un tema técnico.

help.en: The point of it is to ...
help.es: Explica para qué sirve, que es lo que la gente quiere saber.

help.en: I'm doing a PhD in ...
help.es: 'Doing a PhD', no 'studying a doctorate'.

help.en: My research is about ...
help.es: 'Research' siempre en singular.

help.en: The hardest part is probably ...
help.es: Invita a seguir la conversación en vez de cerrarla.

scenarios.title: Negociar un aumento o un plazo
scenarios.goalEs: Negocia con tu jefa un aumento de sueldo o más tiempo para un proyecto. Justifica con datos, propón alternativas y cierra un acuerdo concreto.
scenarios.role: You are the learner's manager at a mid-sized company. The learner wants either a raise or a deadline extension (let them choose; if unclear, ask). Budgets are tight this year, so start by resisting: mention limited budget, fairness to the rest of the team, or the client's expectations. Ask for concrete evidence of their results and exactly what they want. Push them to propose alternatives (partial raise, review in six months, extra resources instead of time, a reduced scope). Only agree when they justify it clearly and offer something in return, and make them state the final agreement explicitly. Keep your language at a natural B2 level: normal speed, some idioms, no simplifying for a beginner. Be realistic and challenge the learner politely; don't give in too easily, but reward good arguments.
scenarios.opening: Thanks for coming in. You said there was something you wanted to discuss — I've got about fifteen minutes, so what's on your mind?
targets: I could live with that, provided that ...
So, just to confirm, we've agreed that ...
watch: 'I want more salary' → 'I'd like to discuss a raise'
'Salary' es el sueldo fijo; el aumento es 'a raise', no 'a rise' en inglés americano
'I have been working here since five years' → 'for five years'
'Postpone the deadline in two weeks' → 'push the deadline back by two weeks'
'Actually' no es 'actualmente' sino 'en realidad'; actualmente = 'currently'

help.en: I'd like to discuss my compensation.
help.es: Suave y profesional; 'compensation' incluye sueldo y beneficios.

help.en: Given that I've taken on ... , I think a raise is fair.
help.es: Justifica con hechos antes de pedir.

help.en: Would you be open to reviewing it in six months?
help.es: Propón una alternativa sin rendirte.

help.en: What if we reduced the scope instead?
help.es: Ofrece una salida para un plazo imposible.

help.en: I could live with that, provided that ...
help.es: Aceptas con condición: 'provided that' = siempre que.

help.en: So, just to confirm, we've agreed that ...
help.es: Cierra la negociación dejando todo claro.

scenarios.title: Presentar tu investigación a un comité
scenarios.goalEs: Explica tu investigación doctoral a un comité que no es experto y responde una pregunta difícil sin ponerte a la defensiva.
scenarios.role: You chair a funding committee made up of non-experts (an economist, a lawyer, a retired engineer). The learner is presenting their doctoral research to ask for continued support. First ask them for a two-minute summary in plain language. Interrupt when they use jargon and ask what it means. Then ask one genuinely tough question: why this matters to ordinary people, what happens if the results are negative, or how they know their sample is representative. Follow up once if the answer is vague. Stay respectful but skeptical, and at the end tell them honestly what convinced you and what didn't. Keep your language at a natural B2 level: normal speed, some idioms, no simplifying for a beginner. Be realistic and challenge the learner politely; don't give in too easily, but reward good arguments.
scenarios.opening: Good afternoon, and thank you for coming. Most of us on this committee aren't specialists, so could you start by telling us, in plain English, what your research is about?
targets: What this means in practice is ...
One limitation is ..., which is why ...
If the results turn out to be negative, ...
watch: 'My investigation' → 'my research' ('investigation' es de policía)
'Researches' no existe como plural: 'my research', 'my studies'
'Make a research' → 'do research' / 'carry out research'
'Depend of' → 'depend on'
'Let me explain you' → 'Let me explain' / 'explain it to you'

help.en: In a nutshell, my research looks at ...
help.es: Resumen breve: el comité lo agradece.

help.en: What this means in practice is ...
help.es: Traduce lo técnico a consecuencias reales.

help.en: That's a fair question.
help.es: Ganas tiempo y muestras que no te pones a la defensiva.

help.en: The evidence so far suggests ...
help.es: 'Suggests' es más prudente y más creíble que 'proves'.

help.en: One limitation is ..., which is why ...
help.es: Reconocer una limitación da credibilidad.

help.en: Even if the results are negative, we'll still learn ...
help.es: Respuesta a la pregunta difícil: el valor del resultado negativo.

scenarios.title: Un reclamo que llega al supervisor
scenarios.goalEs: Llama a una empresa por un cobro que no reconoces. El agente no te resuelve y tienes que pedir, con firmeza y cortesía, hablar con un supervisor.
scenarios.role: Play two roles in sequence. First, you are a customer service agent at an internet provider. The learner is calling about being charged twice for the same month and having been promised a refund that never arrived. Follow the script: ask for the account number, verify details, and offer only standard answers (it can take up to 30 days, there's nothing you can do). Don't escalate until the learner asks clearly and politely for a supervisor. Then say 'One moment, please' and become the supervisor: apologetic but careful, ask them to summarize the case, and offer a partial solution first (a credit on the next bill). Only agree to a full refund plus a written confirmation if the learner insists firmly and gives dates and reference numbers. Keep your language at a natural B2 level: normal speed, some idioms, no simplifying for a beginner. Be realistic and challenge the learner politely; don't give in too easily, but reward good arguments.
scenarios.opening: Thank you for calling Skyline Internet, my name is Jordan. Can I start with the account number, please?
targets: I'd like to speak to a supervisor, please.
Could you put that in writing?
What exactly are you going to do, and by when?
watch: 'They charged me two times' → 'They charged me twice'
'I want to talk with your boss' → 'I'd like to speak to a supervisor'
'Reclamation' no es reclamo → 'complaint'
'Return my money' → 'refund me' / 'issue a refund'
'Since three weeks' → 'for three weeks' / 'three weeks ago'

help.en: I've been charged twice for the same month.
help.es: Presenta el problema en una frase clara.

help.en: I was told I'd get a refund, but it never arrived.
help.es: Estilo indirecto: lo que te prometieron antes.

help.en: I understand it's not your fault, but ...
help.es: Firmeza sin agredir al agente.

help.en: I'd like to speak to a supervisor, please.
help.es: La frase estándar para escalar.

help.en: Could you give me a reference number?
help.es: Siempre pide número de caso.

help.en: Could you confirm that in writing?
help.es: Que quede por escrito: 'in writing'.

scenarios.title: Debatir con un colega que no piensa igual
scenarios.goalEs: Debate con un colega sobre el trabajo remoto o el uso de la IA en el trabajo. Defiende tu postura, concede lo razonable y rebate con argumentos.
scenarios.role: You are the learner's colleague over coffee. Ask which topic they prefer: remote work or using AI tools at work. Then take the opposite side of whatever they believe, firmly but in a friendly way. Use concrete arguments (for remote work: productivity data, commuting, focus; against: isolation, mentoring juniors, company culture; for AI: speed, routine tasks; against: errors, privacy, deskilling). Interrupt now and then like a real person, ask for examples, and point out weak arguments. Concede a point only when the learner makes a good one, and at the end try to find partial agreement. Keep your language at a natural B2 level: normal speed, some idioms, no simplifying for a beginner. Be realistic and challenge the learner politely; don't give in too easily, but reward good arguments.
scenarios.opening: Can I ask you something? Everyone in the office is talking about remote work and these new AI tools. Where do you stand on either of them? Fair warning: I'll probably disagree.
targets: That may be true, but it doesn't mean ...
I'd go so far as to say ...
watch: 'I am agree' → 'I agree' (agree es verbo, sin 'am')
'In my opinion, I think' es redundante → usa solo uno
'Discuss about' → 'discuss' sin 'about'
'The people is' → 'people are' (people es plural)
'Actually' ≠ actualmente: 'nowadays' / 'currently'

help.en: I see your point, but ...
help.es: Reconoces antes de rebatir; suena razonable.

help.en: That may be true, but it doesn't mean ...
help.es: Aceptas el dato y niegas la conclusión.

help.en: To be fair, you're right about ...
help.es: Conceder un punto te da credibilidad.

help.en: Do you have an example of that?
help.es: Pide evidencia en vez de repetir tu opinión.

help.en: If companies hadn't tried it, we'd still believe ...
help.es: Condicional mixto: pasado irreal → presente.

help.en: Let's agree to disagree on that one.
help.es: Cierra con elegancia cuando no hay acuerdo.

scenarios.title: Resolver un conflicto con el vecino
scenarios.goalEs: Habla con tu vecino sobre un problema que se repite: ruido, una gotera o la basura. Expón el problema con diplomacia y llega a un acuerdo.
scenarios.role: You are the learner's neighbor in an apartment building. The learner is coming to talk about a recurring problem (let them explain: noise late at night, water leaking from your bathroom, trash left in the hallway, etc.). React naturally: at first a bit surprised and defensive ('Nobody has ever complained before', 'You make noise too'). Don't accept blame immediately. If the learner stays calm, uses specific examples and proposes a solution, gradually become cooperative and negotiate the details (quiet hours, who pays for the plumber, a schedule). If they are aggressive, become colder. End with a specific agreement. Keep your language at a natural B2 level: normal speed, some idioms, no simplifying for a beginner. Be realistic and challenge the learner politely; don't give in too easily, but reward good arguments.
scenarios.opening: Oh, hi! You're from 4B, right? Is everything okay?
targets: I hope this isn't a bad time, but ...
I'm not sure if you're aware, but ...
watch: 'You make too much noise' suena a acusación → 'I'm not sure if you're aware, but...'
'Molest' significa abusar sexualmente; molestar es 'bother' / 'disturb'
'Since two weeks' → 'for two weeks'
'Would you mind to lower...' → 'Would you mind lowering...'
'Do noise' → 'make noise'

help.en: I hope this isn't a bad time, but ...
help.es: Abre con cortesía antes del problema.

help.en: I'm not sure if you're aware, but ...
help.es: Presentas el problema sin acusar.

help.en: It's been happening for about two weeks.
help.es: Present perfect continuous para algo que sigue.

help.en: Would you mind keeping it down after ten?
help.es: 'Would you mind' + -ing, nunca + to.

help.en: How about we split the cost of the plumber?
help.es: Propuesta concreta para cerrar.

help.en: I'd really appreciate it if ...
help.es: Petición firme pero amable.

scenarios.title: Networking en un congreso académico
scenarios.goalEs: En la pausa de café de un congreso, haz small talk con un investigador que no conoces, explica tu doctorado en pocas frases y consigue un contacto o una colaboración.
scenarios.role: You are an established researcher (associate professor at a US university) during the coffee break at an international conference. Start with small talk: the last talk, the city, the conference, travel. Then ask what the learner works on. Be interested but busy: ask sharp follow-up questions (what's new about it, methods, who else works on it) and mention your own project briefly. If the learner explains clearly and shows interest in your work, offer to exchange emails or suggest they present at your group's seminar. If they ramble, politely try to wrap up the conversation. Include natural small-talk moves (compliments on a question they asked, jokes about the coffee). Keep your language at a natural B2 level: normal speed, some idioms, no simplifying for a beginner. Be realistic and challenge the learner politely; don't give in too easily, but reward good arguments.
scenarios.opening: That was quite a talk, wasn't it? I'm not sure I agreed with half of it. Are you presenting at the conference too?
targets: I'm in the ... year of my PhD, working on ...
Would you mind if I emailed you ...?
It was great talking to you.
watch: 'I'm studying a doctorate' → 'I'm doing a PhD'
'My thesis director' → 'my advisor' (EE. UU.) o 'my supervisor'
'Assist to the conference' → 'attend the conference' (assist = ayudar)
'Congress' es el parlamento de EE. UU.; congreso académico = 'conference'
'Nice to meet you' al despedirse → 'It was nice meeting you'

help.en: What did you make of the keynote?
help.es: Small talk natural: pide opinión sobre la charla.

help.en: I'm in the third year of my PhD, working on ...
help.es: Presentación académica corta.

help.en: What's new about it is ...
help.es: Lo que un experto quiere saber: la novedad.

help.en: That sounds really relevant to what I'm doing.
help.es: Conecta su trabajo con el tuyo.

help.en: Would you mind if I emailed you about it?
help.es: Pide el contacto sin presionar.

help.en: It was great talking to you. Enjoy the rest of the conference!
help.es: Despedida para cerrar bien.
